data.case_title: Landlord's termination of tenancy (Kündigung wegen Eigenbedarf) – Vegesacker Heerstraße 140
data.summary: Your landlord Hinrich Musterlesum has given written notice ending your tenancy of the attic flat at Vegesacker Heerstraße 140 because he wants to live there himself (Eigenbedarf). The tenancy ends on 31 August 2027, and you may object on hardship grounds (§§574–574b BGB) if the objection reaches him by 30 June 2027.
data.explanation: Your landlord is ending your lease because he and his wife want to move into your flat themselves, since they can no longer manage the stairs in their current home. The tenancy is set to end on 31 August 2027. German law gives you the right, under §§574–574b BGB, to object if moving out would be an unreasonable hardship for you or your family and ask for the tenancy to continue; such an objection must be made in writing (text form) and must reach the landlord by the deadline shown. You don't have to decide immediately, but you should consider whether a hardship objection applies to you — talking to a tenants' association (Mieterverein) or a lawyer can help — and start looking for a new home in good time in any case.

items.action: If moving out would be a hardship for you or your family, send the landlord a written objection (Widerspruch) in text form before the deadline, requesting continuation of the tenancy.
items.consequence: If no objection reaches the landlord by the deadline, you lose the statutory right to request continuation of the tenancy on hardship grounds and the tenancy ends as given notice.
